newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian Socialists dismiss opposition protests.
newsitem.headline: Serbian Socialists dismiss opposition protests.

text.p: Serbia's ruling Socialists on Thursday said an opposition coalition had "prematurely" declared victory in local elections and dismissed its protests, the state news agency Tanjug reported.
In the first public response to a wave of opposition demonstrations this week, the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) dismissed opposition demands to confirm election results in a number of major towns.
"Why such a hurry for the results to be proclaimed before the entire electoral procedure is brought to a close?" SPS spokesman Ivica Dacic was quoted as saying by Tanjug.
The Socialist party was "calmly awaiting the end of the electoral procedure, certain that the results will faithfully reflect the will of the citizens...," he said.
The opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition claimed victory in a number of major towns across the country in run-off municipal elections held on Sunday.
Authorities confirmed the opposition victory in the capital Belgrade -- an unprecedented defeat for the Socialists led by President Slobodan Milosevic.
But local electoral commissions in other towns failed to announce final results by Tuesday evening as required by law.
The commissions, dominated by the Socialists, have cited a large number of unspecified irregularities and ordered another round of voting in towns where the opposition says it won.
Opposition leaders have accused the authorities of committing extensive fraud to alter the results.
Although Dacic accused the opposition of jumping to conclusions, he said that it was "definite" that the SPS won a majority of city council seats in three-quarters of all municipalities.
